FINAL CREDENTIALS AND VARIABLES AUDIT — VERIFY AND FINISH NOW

Rork already has the required credentials.
IVX Variables already contains approximately 12 configured credentials/secrets.

Do not ask the owner to resend credentials.
Do not claim credentials are missing without runtime proof.
Do not stop at a narrative report.

Your job now is to audit, bind, test, correct, and verify every credential end to end.

==================================================
1. AUDIT ALL EXISTING IVX VARIABLES
==================================================

Inspect every configured IVX Variable/Secret and create a safe inventory.

For each variable return:

- masked variable name
- service
- environment
- where it is stored
- where it is expected to be injected
- runtime process that uses it
- loaded: yes/no
- empty: yes/no
- malformed: yes/no
- active: yes/no
- last verified timestamp
- safe test performed
- HTTP status
- result
- exact blocker if any

Do not expose secret values.

==================================================
2. VERIFY THE 12 CORE CREDENTIAL GROUPS
==================================================

Audit all credentials currently configured for:

1. GitHub
2. Render
3. Supabase URL
4. Supabase anon key
5. Supabase service-role key
6. Supabase access token
7. Supabase database URL
8. Expo/EAS
9. Android signing/keystore
10. Apple/iOS build credentials
11. AWS/SMS
12. Any production AI/API provider used by IVX IA

Also audit any additional configured variable discovered.

==================================================
3. VERIFY RUNTIME BINDING
==================================================

For every credential verify all required runtime locations:

- Rork execution environment
- Render service
- GitHub Actions
- EAS build profile
- Expo public configuration
- backend server
- production web
- Android build
- iOS build
- autonomous worker runtime
- Owner Auth Guardian
- SMS alert service
- database migration runner

A credential existing in Variables is not enough.

It must be proven that the correct runtime process receives and uses it.

==================================================
4. RUN SAFE LIVE TESTS
==================================================

Perform safe service-specific tests.

GITHUB
- authenticate
- read owner repository
- verify branch access
- verify push access
- verify workflow permission
- verify release permission

RENDER
- authenticate
- read correct service
- read deploy status
- read deployed SHA
- verify environment binding

SUPABASE
- verify project
- verify auth
- verify database connection
- verify storage
- verify service-role server-side access
- verify migration connection
- verify RLS inspection capability

EAS / EXPO
- verify account
- verify project ID
- verify build permission
- verify Android build access
- verify iOS build access

ANDROID SIGNING
- verify keystore exists
- verify alias binding
- verify signing pipeline
- verify release APK can be signed

APPLE / IOS
- verify team/project binding
- verify build credentials
- verify signing readiness
- verify EAS iOS build capability

AWS / SMS
- verify AWS credential binding
- verify region
- verify SMS service permission
- send one safe test SMS
- confirm message ID
- confirm delivery status

AI/API PROVIDERS
- verify authentication
- verify allowed model/service
- verify rate-limit status
- verify server-side use only

==================================================
5. CREDENTIAL DECISION RULE
==================================================

Never ask the owner for credentials unless a real runtime test proves one of the following:

- variable absent
- variable empty
- invalid format
- expired
- revoked
- wrong project
- wrong account
- insufficient permission
- HTTP 401
- HTTP 403

For every failure show:

Service:
Variable name:
Runtime:
Test performed:
HTTP status:
Error code:
Safe error message:
Required correction:

If the credential exists but is not injected correctly, fix the binding.
Do not ask for the credential again.

==================================================
6. FIX ALL BINDING FAILURES
==================================================

Correct:

- wrong variable names
- duplicate variable names
- stale variables
- variables in the wrong environment
- server secrets exposed to mobile
- missing Render injection
- missing GitHub Actions secrets
- missing EAS environment mapping
- missing migration runtime binding
- wrong Supabase project reference
- wrong AWS region
- wrong GitHub token selected
- old or shadowed credentials
- development credentials in production
- production credentials missing from release builds

After each correction, rerun the same live test.

==================================================
7. SECURITY AUDIT
==================================================

Verify:

- no secret is committed to source
- no password is in fixtures
- no service-role key is in mobile/web bundles
- no token appears in logs
- no credentials appear in screenshots
- old exposed credentials are rotated when required
- new credentials are stored only in secure secret stores
- secret scanning passes
- APK bundle scan passes
- web bundle scan passes
- Git history is reviewed for exposures

Do not rotate a production credential without owner approval unless it has already been exposed and emergency policy explicitly allows automatic rotation.

==================================================
8. FINISH THE CURRENT BLOCKERS
==================================================

Resolve and verify now:

- AWS/SMS runtime binding
- GitHub workflow scope
- SUPABASE_DB_URL binding
- Android release keystore
- EAS Android build
- EAS iOS build readiness
- Render API access
- Supabase password reset email configuration
- production migration runner
- Autonomous Dashboard credential status
- Owner Auth Guardian credential status

Do not leave these marked BLOCKED if the needed credentials already exist.

==================================================
9. UPDATE THE AUTONOMOUS DASHBOARD
==================================================

Add a live Credentials and Integrations section showing:

- service
- masked variable name
- environment
- binding status
- last runtime test
- last HTTP status
- permission status
- security status
- blocker
- assigned worker
- repair job
- final result

Do not show secret values.

==================================================
10. FINAL VERIFIED OUTPUT
==================================================

Return one final matrix:

Service | Variable | Stored | Injected | Authenticated | Permission Test | Runtime Test | Security Check | Final Status

Also return:

- total variables found
- total valid
- total binding failures
- total permission failures
- total corrected
- total still blocked
- exact remaining blockers
- files changed
- commits
- deployments
- test evidence
- dashboard screenshot

FINAL STATUS RULE

VERIFIED only when:

- every required credential is found
- every credential is bound to the correct runtime
- every service authenticates successfully
- required permissions pass
- no secrets are exposed
- current blockers are cleared
- the Autonomous Dashboard reflects the real status

If any credential fails, report PARTIAL with exact runtime evidence.

Start now.
Do not ask for credentials again unless a real test returns missing, 401, or 403.
Audit all IVX Variables and finish the integrations end to end.
